06/10/2026 15:25 — WhatsApp Calling API Checked

**Yes, partner. I checked the current documentation. It is real, and my previous answer was directionally correct.** Meta explicitly says the **WhatsApp Calling API lets businesses initiate and receive voice calls through the WhatsApp Business Platform**. Meta published a Calling API implementation video in June 2026. citeturn1search0turn1search7

### What is actually possible

| Requirement | WhatsApp Calling API |
|---|---|
| Customer calls business on WhatsApp | ✅ Yes |
| Business answers programmatically | ✅ Yes |
| Business calls customer on WhatsApp | ✅ Yes, with permission |
| Customer grants ongoing call permission | ✅ Supported |
| Real-time audio | ✅ WebRTC/VoIP |
| SIP integration | ✅ Supported |
| IVR / keypad DTMF | ✅ Supported |
| AI voice agent | **✅ Yes — architecture supports it** |
| Normal PSTN phone call | ❌ Different thing |
| WhatsApp → normal telephone number | ❌ Not directly |
| Recording | ⚠️ Your voice infrastructure/application layer |
| Call analytics | ✅ |
| User-initiated call cost | **Free at Meta calling layer** |
| Business-initiated calls | 💰 Charged based on duration/country |

Meta specifically describes businesses using **AI assistants with WhatsApp voice calling** for scaled customer support. citeturn1search1

### Most important point for TalkProof

This is more interesting than I initially thought.

You **do not necessarily need Retell AI just to get the WhatsApp audio**.

The direct architecture can be:

```text
CUSTOMER
   │
   │ WhatsApp Voice Call
   ▼
WHATSAPP
   │
   │ Calling API
   │ WebRTC / SIP
   ▼
TALKPROOF VOICE GATEWAY
   │
   ├──► STT
   │
   ├──► TalkProof conversation/orchestration
   │       │
   │       ├── RAG / Knowledge Base
   │       ├── LLM
   │       ├── Lead qualification
   │       ├── CRM
   │       ├── Scheduling
   │       └── Escalation
   │
   ├──► TTS
   │
   ▼
WhatsApp Calling API
   │
   ▼
CUSTOMER
```

Meta's underlying media connection uses **WebRTC**. For an outbound call, for example, the business supplies a WebRTC offer and receives the SDP answer through the calling flow. citeturn1search4

And there is another significant option:

```text
WhatsApp
    │
    ▼
   SIP
    │
    ├───────────────┐
    ▼               ▼
TalkProof       Voice provider
Voice Engine    / Contact centre
```

Meta documentation supports **SIP as an alternative signalling integration**. citeturn1search3

### Outbound has an important restriction

You **cannot simply take 10,000 mobile numbers and start WhatsApp-calling them.**

The WhatsApp user must first give the business permission to call. Meta supports several permission mechanisms, including a permission-request message and callback permission after the customer has called the business. citeturn1search4

So:

```text
WhatsApp message
      ↓
"Allow this business to call me?"
      ↓
Customer allows
      ↓
TalkProof can initiate WhatsApp call
      ↓
AI / human conversation
```

That's very different from ordinary outbound PSTN dialling.

### And Twilio already supports this

Interestingly, urlTwilio's WhatsApp Business Calling documentationturn1search2 confirms both inbound and outbound WhatsApp calling.

But there's a major boundary: **Twilio says WhatsApp endpoints cannot be bridged to PSTN endpoints.** citeturn1search2

So we shouldn't model WhatsApp as merely another telephone carrier.

I would model it in TalkProof as:

```text
                  TALKPROOF
                      │
          ┌───────────┼────────────┐
          │           │            │
        PSTN       WhatsApp      Future
          │           │          channels
     Twilio/       Meta
      Exotel     Calling API
          │           │
          └─────┬─────┘
                ▼
          VOICE ENGINE
                │
        ┌───────┼────────┐
       STT     Agent     TTS
                │
              RAG/LLM
```

This fits extremely well with the carrier abstraction work you've already been doing in TalkProof: **WhatsApp Calling should be investigated as a first-class voice channel, not bolted onto the existing WhatsApp messaging adapter.** memcite

06/10/2026 15:23 — WhatsApp API Voice Calls

**Yes — but with an important distinction.**

If you mean the official **WhatsApp Business Platform / Cloud API**, Meta now supports **WhatsApp Business Calling**, so a business can support voice calls with customers through WhatsApp. It isn't simply the same as sending a WhatsApp message via an API.

For something like **TalkProof**, the architecture could potentially become:

**Customer WhatsApp → WhatsApp Business Calling → your voice backend → AI voice agent → STT → LLM/RAG → TTS → customer**

So potentially, instead of:

**Phone → Twilio/Exotel/Retell → TalkProof**

you could have another channel:

**WhatsApp Call → Meta calling infrastructure → TalkProof voice/AI layer**

There are restrictions around **who can initiate calls, user permission/consent, account eligibility, supported countries, and how the calling API is integrated**. These details have changed over time.

If you're considering this for TalkProof, I can check the **current October 2026 Meta WhatsApp Calling API documentation** and determine exactly:

**Inbound call | Outbound call | AI agent | WebRTC/SIP | recording | India/UK availability | pricing | Retell/Vapi integration | direct TalkProof integration**

That would tell us whether WhatsApp can become a real **additional TalkProof carrier/channel**, rather than assuming it works like Twilio.
